Bold comic-book ink style, heavy linework, red and blue-black palette, night city. Use <Picture 2> and <Picture 1> as reference frames and <Audio 1> exactly as it is.
CUT 1: top-down view of the little boy superhero on the rooftop — red cape fluttering in the wind, hands planted on his hips, freckles and a cocky grin as he looks straight up into the camera. The camera slowly descends toward him as he delivers his line — as he speaks, comic-book graphic overlay text word by word in sync with his voice: "GET READY TO" - "MEET" — "YOUR" — "MAKER" — huge jagged comic lettering, white with heavy black outlines and red drop shadows, tilted at scrappy angles, until the three words hang stacked in the air above him between his face and the lens.
TRANSITION: a violent WHIP PAN off the rooftop that SMEARS the floating words away with it, motion-streaked —
CUT 2: low hero angle on the colossal black mech-kaiju towering over the skyline as it rears back and unleashes a GIANT terrifying ROAR — jaws wide with fangs, red eyes and chest-core flaring blinding bright, blue lightning arcing off its head, the roar's shockwave rippling dust and rattling windows down the buildings, comic-style speed-lines and ink splatter bursting from the impact of the sound. It leans INTO the camera as the roar peaks. Hold on the roar.

---

A dim office. Mulder leaning against his desk.
MULDER: Scully, there's something I never told you.
SCULLY: (bracing herself) What now, Mulder.
MULDER: I have a man-gina.
SCULLY: ...That's it? After everything we've seen, THAT'S your confession?

Chaplin steps in first twirling his cane and cheerfully saying, "My word, look at this place!" Bogart follows adjusting his fedora and grumbling, "Quiet, kid." Reeves walks in calm and cool, nodding to say, "Whoa." Chalamet trails last in a modern bright suit, smiling and saying, "Vibes are immaculate." Continuous smooth camera movement tracking backward as they enter, natural indoor lighting, ambient room tone, and clear synchronized dialogue.

<Subject 1> is a human character replacing the cartoon pig from <Video 1>, occupying the same position, framing, and role in each shot.

[video editing + audio reuse] The target video is an edited version of <Video 1>. The cartoon pig is replaced by <Subject 1>, a human character, in the same position and performing the same actions across all shots. <Subject 1> speaks the line "That's the end" in a high-pitched voice, replacing the pig's original vocal performance while the rest of <Audio 1> is retained.

<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): attribute_transfer - the pig's position, motion, and screen role are transferred to a human character.
<Audio 1>: partially_copy - the original audio track is retained except for the pig's dialogue, which is replaced with the new line performed in a high-pitched voice.

detailed_description:
The target video keeps the original live-action/cartoon-composite style and lighting of <Video 1>.
[Shot 1] The scene from <Video 1> is preserved in composition and camera movement, but the cartoon pig is replaced by <Subject 1>, a human character standing/positioned exactly where the pig was, matching its posture and motion. <Subject 1> (S1) turns toward the camera and says, in a high-pitched voice, <d>[English] That's the end.</d> All other visual elements, background, and framing from <Video 1> remain unchanged.

overall_soundscape:
The ambient sound from <Audio 1> continues underneath the dialogue, unchanged from the original.

N/A

Make sure you use correct sizes divisilble by 32 e.g. 1920 x 1088 not 1920 x 1080. It will scale it down but it will mess up the first frames of results and not honour the FF ref image accurately. div by 32 is VERY IMPORTANT for results at higher res I am finding.

model was trained at 1344 x 768 (1 mp /32) but above that I get better clarity (at 2mp but it takes ages).

with Light2xv lora best results at 2mp (1920 x 1088 NOT x 1080) but takes 25 mins at 4 steps. needs the vram control nodes in else you oom. 

was able to do 16:9 1.4mp (1600 × 900) in 25 mins, 8 steps with Qrusher lora. Was improved but still slight breaking. Light2xv was faster but quality less good until 2 mp.

nodes.title: Note: MiniMax H3
widgets_values:
## MiniMax H3

[MiniMax H3](https://www.minimax.io/blog/minimax-h3) is MiniMax's general-purpose, omni-modal generation model. It jointly understands text, image, video, and audio, and generates video with **native stereo audio**: voice, sound effects, and music are modeled jointly in a single forward pass, not layered on afterward. Output is up to 2K resolution, 24fps, and up to about 15 seconds.

## ComfyUI links
- [ComfyUI#15224](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/15224)
- [🤗 Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3)

## About this workflow

This template runs the **reference-to-video (ref2va)** task using the `MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo` node. It takes any mix of reference images, videos, and standalone audio, and weaves them into the generation to lock in a character's identity, a style, a motion, a camera move, or a voice.

**Key inputs**

- **ref_images / ref_videos / ref_video_audios / ref_audios**: up to 9 reference images, 3 reference videos (each may carry its own paired soundtrack), and 3 standalone reference audio clips
- **prompt**: reference the inputs by tag, in the exact order they were connected, for example `<Picture 1>`, `<Video 1>`, `<Audio 1>`, then describe the target scene, motion, and audio
- **ref_image_size**: `match` scales references down to the generation's resolution (faster); `max` keeps up to a 2048px short edge for stronger identity fidelity, at the cost of speed since reference tokens ride along every sampling step
- **width / height**: set via Resolution Selector.
- **duration (seconds)**: converted to a valid frame `length` by the Math Expression node

**Sampling and decode**

- Sampler: `res_multistep`. `beta` or `normal` scheduler tends to outperform `simple` for reference-heavy prompts like this one
- The sampler's joint audio+video `LATENT` output feeds directly into both `VAEDecode` (video, `minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16`) and `VAEDecodeAudio` (audio, `minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32`); each decode node automatically pulls its own half out of the packed latent. `CreateVideo` then muxes the two into a single MP4 with synced sound
- The diffusion model here is `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors`, a different set of weights from the `fl2va` model used by the t2v/i2v templates

Ref2va's output is very sensitive to prompt wording; matching the reference tags precisely and being explicit about which reference drives which part of the shot tends to work best.

# Mark DK Berry dot com

**Patreon**: [https://www.patreon.com/c/AIMakingMovies](https://www.patreon.com/c/AIMakingMovies)

**YT**: [https://www.youtube.com/@markdkberry](https://www.youtube.com/@markdkberry)

---

## SPEED UPS

Everyone is trying to figure out best things for speed ups

Kijai is suggesting Sage Atnn (2.2) -> Patch Sol-Attn (mostly tested on Blackwell only) -> Easycache (gives me >50% speed up but at quality loss)

Minimax the developers clearly agree - [https://x.com/MiniMax_AI/status/2084745241589080491](https://x.com/MiniMax_AI/status/2084745241589080491)

A patch sol attn for 3060s specifically is here, and I have installed it but still not seeing much difference yet [https://github.com/Apache0ne/ComfyUI-fasterminimax](https://github.com/Apache0ne/ComfyUI-fasterminimax)

Sol explainer:

```
tau: controls the sparsity, higher = faster = poorer quality
start/end percent self explanatory, outside the range it will run whatever other attention you have patched like sage
min_tokens to filter small layers since no benefit there
int8_qk can be faster at low tau, no effect at higher
sink_cond important for H3 to avoid messing audio/conds
morton is better quality when it works, when not it causes blocky artifacts, experimental
```



**Some notes on what Sage Att, Mem Eff, Sol and Easycache do from Kijai**: 

*"Sage is minimal quality loss, "mem eff" on top of that just reduces peak VRAM use a bit, sol and cache methods are quality/speed compromises. Of course like with any speed improvement, you then have room to possibly improve other aspects like resolution. So "quality" is pretty relative"*

widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the hotel elevator lobby environment in <Picture 1>, featuring gold-toned elevator doors set into a polished marble wall, with warm ambient overhead lighting.
<Subject 2> is the man in <Picture 2>, with medium-length brown hair, wearing a jacket and jeans.
<Subject 3> is the blonde woman in <Picture 3>, wearing a blue dress.
<Subject 4> is the brunette woman in <Picture 4>, wearing a black leather top and leather pants.
<Subject 5> is the Black woman in <Picture 5>, wearing a leopard-print dress.

summary:
[reference generation] The target video shows <Subject 2>, <Subject 3>, <Subject 4>, and <Subject 5> standing together in <Subject 1>, waiting for the elevator, then stepping inside together as the gold doors open, with the camera panning to a frontal view before the doors close on the group.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the gold-toned elevator doors, polished marble wall, and warm overhead lighting are retained throughout.
<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the man's medium-length brown hair, jacket, and jeans are retained.
<Subject 3> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the blonde woman's hair and blue dress are retained.
<Subject 4> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the brunette woman's hair, black leather top, and leather pants are retained.
<Subject 5> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the woman's leopard-print dress is retained.

detailed_description:
The target video is in a realistic, cinematic style with warm, upscale lighting and smooth continuous camera motion.
[Shot 1] The scene opens in <Subject 1>, the hotel elevator lobby, its gold-toned doors set into a polished marble wall under warm ambient overhead light. <Subject 2>, the man with medium-length brown hair in a jacket and jeans, stands closest to the doors. Beside him stands <Subject 3>, the blonde woman in a blue dress. Next to her stands <Subject 4>, the brunette woman in a black leather top and leather pants. Completing the group, <Subject 5>, the woman in a leopard-print dress, stands at the far end. All four face the gold doors, waiting, exchanging occasional small glances between one another. The gold doors slide open smoothly, and the group steps forward together into the elevator car, filling the frame as the doors close behind them off-camera. The camera slowly arcs around from a side angle to a frontal position, facing directly into the elevator, as everyone inside turns in unison to face the camera. The gold doors then slide closed, sealing the group inside, and the shot ends on the closed doors.

overall_soundscape:
Soft ambient hotel-lobby room tone continues throughout, with the mechanical hum and chime of the elevator doors opening and closing, and the faint shuffle of footsteps as the group steps forward.

non_diegetic_music:
A subtle, understated ambient score with soft sustained tones, audible only to the audience, underscoring the scene without swelling.

widgets_values:
SPEED UP LORAS

As of 9th August 2026 

without lora use default 20 steps and res_multistep/simple (up to 50 steps if you can and want improvements). 

with turbo loras (drBaphs/Qrusher) (euler/beta) steps 8 to 12 is sweet spot currently but maybe 4 once they have finished training them. (currently I set str 1.8) 1344 x 768 8 steps finishes in 15, 12 steps in 22 mins.

For 2mp use Lightx2v lora from Kijai with 4 steps (25 mins for 5 seconds of video) best results by far so far at that resolution. (I've been using 6 steps, 0.5 str. the intended strength using KJ conversions is 0.5)

Testing silveroxides (with adaln_proj script fix) as well for 4 steps. str 1 feels to strong, 0.8 as middle ground. This is fastest and good but different strenghts changes the camera position too much and str 0.5 added duplicate people in.

for lower resolution I prefer Qrusher or better still DrBaph turbo lora and use 8 steps.

In all cases so far I stuck to Euler/beta originally then switched to er_sde later.
